text:
maria: Nightdash alert - small-batch p95 jumped ~30% starting 02:00 UTC after today's merge. https://dash.internal/nightdash/abc123 (snapshot attached)
nightdash-bot: alert: p95_small_batch > 200ms (baseline 150ms) - 3 consecutive windows
maria: rollback not automatic yet, but we should triage. @aj @chandra @leo
aj: grabbing flamegraphs now. can anyone repro locally with batch=1 latency profile?
chandra: I ran microbench on staging; repros. CPU-side profiles show more time in kernel_selector::choose() and then prefetch path where we miss kv cache more often.
aj: interesting. any recent kernel selection changes in last PRs? commit d3f2a9b modified prober timestamp ordering for probe fairness.
maria: that change was intended to fix long-tail in big-batch, might've regressed small-batch.
becka: paste of perf summary:
```
cmd: ./perf-run --bench small-batch --model llama2
p95 before: 138ms
p95 after: 190ms
hot spots:
 - kernel_selector::score() +14%
 - prefetcher::issue_prefetch +22%
 - kv_cache::lookup miss rate +4%
```
aj: the +4% kv miss could explain token-level gap. but score +14% points to selector making different kernel choices.
chandra: dumping trace, here's a snippet - prober timestamps are non-monotonic across async probes, kernel prober sorts by timestamp then picks kernel; with skew we pick slower kernel more often.
leo: that could be due to clock skew introduced by scheduling change in scheduler thread; the reorder avoids starvation but broke ordering for probes issued near context switch boundaries.
maria: can we bisect to the commit? if it's d3f2a9b we should try reverting locally and run nightly perf job.
aj: starting bisection — running CI microbench: `./ci/run_bench --commit d3f2a9b` will take ~15m
infra-bot: CI job 82734 started by aj, target: perf/microbench/small-batch
becka: also capturing KV heatmap; will upload in 10
aj: CI shows perf back to baseline on revert candidate. p95 140ms.
maria: ok rollback hold for rollout. filing rollout hold ticket and tagging release manager @simon
maria: simon can you hold the rollout? we need a revert or a targeted fix to prober ordering.
simon: holding rollout. moving to blocked state. thanks.
chandra: proposed fix: keep prober timestamp ordering but de-noise timestamps by bumping microsecond granularity using monotonic counter in prober; PR ready: https://git.internal/r/redwood/changes/PR-6754
aj: looks good, running bench on PR-6754
nightdash-bot: update: alert resolved on canary with PR-6754, p95 back within baseline after 3 windows :white_check_mark:
maria: great. next steps: merge fix, patch release, revert hold, add regression test to CI that runs small-batch microbench on merge.
becka: logging the kv heatmap and attaching profiler. I'll drop artifacts in the ticket.
chandra: +1 on regression test. Also let's add a unit for prober timestamp monotonicity.
maria: thanks team. I'll follow up with postmortem link tomorrow.
